'''Kenneth Irwin Gross''' (14 October 1938 – 10 September 2017) was an American mathematician.

Born in [[Malden, Massachusetts]] in 1938,<ref>biographical information ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> Gross received from [[Brandeis University]] his bachelor's degree in 1960 and his master's degree in 1962. He received his Ph.D. in 1966 from [[Washington University in St. Louis]] under [[Ray Kunze]] with thesis ''Plancherel Transform of the Nilpotent Part of <math>G_2</math> and Some Applications to the Representation Theory of <math>G_2</math>''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=2159}}  {{cite journal|title=Plancherel Transform of the Nilpotent Part of <math>G_2</math> and Some Applications to the Representation Theory of <math>G_2</math>|journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=132|year=1968|pages=411–446|jstor=1994851|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1968-0233933-6|doi-access=free}}</ref> He was an assistant professor from 1966 to 1968 at [[Tulane University]] and an assistant professor from 1968 to 1973 at [[Dartmouth College]]. He became in 1973 an associate professor and eventually a full professor at the [[University of North Carolina]] before resigning in 1981. From 1981 to 1985 he was the chair of the mathematics department of the [[University of Wyoming]]. In 1988 Gross became a professor at the [[University of Vermont]], where he served as chair of the department of mathematics and statistics from 1988 to 1992. On a leave of absence he was for two years (2003–2005) at [[Lesley University]], where he developed the mathematics program.

Gross has been a visiting professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]], the [[University of Utah]], the Academia Sinica in Taiwan, [[Drexel University]], [[Macquarie University]], and Australia's [[University of Newcastle (Australia)|University of Newcastle]]. He has twice served as a divisional program director for the [[National Science Foundation]]. He was the director of the Vermont Mathematics Initiative.<ref>[http://www.uvm.edu/~vmi/ Vermont Mathematics Initiative] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150510231326/http://www.uvm.edu/~vmi/ |date=2015-05-10 }}</ref>

He did research on [[harmonic analysis]], [[group representation theory]], analysis on [[Lie group]]s and [[homogeneous space]]s, [[special function]]s, [[Fourier analysis]], and mathematical applications to physics and [[multivariate statistics]].

In 1979 he received the [[Lester Randolph Ford Award]].<ref name="GrossEvolutionHarmonicAnalysis">{{cite journal | last=Gross | first=Kenneth I. | title=On the Evolution of Noncommutative Harmonic Analysis | journal=The American Mathematical Monthly | publisher=Taylor & Francis | volume=85 | issue=7 | year=1978 | issn=0002-9890 | doi=10.1080/00029890.1978.11994636 | pages=525–548}}</ref> In 1981 he received the [[Chauvenet Prize]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=On the Evolution of Noncommutative Harmonic Analysis|journal=American Mathematical Monthly|volume=85|year=1978|pages=525–548|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/on-the-evolution-of-noncommutative-harmonic-analysis-0|doi=10.2307/2320861|jstor=2320861|last1=Gross|first1=Kenneth I.|issue=7}}</ref> In 2008 he received a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2024-10-07|archive-date=2024-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-05-06.</ref> He died on 10 September 2017 at the age of 78.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevendaysvt.com/vermont/obituary-kenneth-irwin-gross-1938-2017/Content?oid=8059550|title=Obituary: Kenneth Irwin Gross, 1938-2017}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*as editor: The mathematics of energy research, SIAM 1984
*with [[Donald St. P. Richards]]: {{cite journal|title=Hypergeometric functions on complex matrix space|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=1991|volume=24|pages=349–355|mr=1071029|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1991-16031-3|doi-access=free|last1=Gross|first1=Kenneth I.|last2=Richards|first2=Donald St. P.|issue=2}}
*Harmonic Analysis, Encyclopedia of the History and Philosophy of the Mathematical Sciences, Routledge, 1994, vol. 1, pp.&nbsp;395–418
*as editor with D.S.P. Richards, P. Sally, T. Ton-That ''Representation theory and harmonic analysis'', Contemporary Mathematics, vol. 191, American Mathematical Society 1995
*editor with R. Ewing, C. Martin: The Merging of Disciplines: New Directions in Pure, Applied, and Computational Mathematics, Springer Verlag 1986
